In brief

After a brief prologue in the unfamiliar style of a woman's sentimental novel, and a much longer section employing the free indirect speech of Joyce's "initial style" (but now centered for the first time on a woman), Nausicaa concludes in a most familiar style when Bloom's voice enters: "Poor girl! That's why she's left on the shelf and the others did a sprint. Thought something was wrong by the cut of her jib." Like Stephen in Proteus, he is alone on the beach, doing pretty much nothing, and the narrative consists almost entirely of interior monologue. But one thing is new. Night is falling, Bloom is getting sleepy, and he looks back over many of the experiences and thoughts he has had throughout the day. This kind of retrospective organization will reappear in later chapters: Circe, Ithaca, Penelope.

At more length

Every chapter in which Bloom has played a role contributes memories to his monologue on the beach: Calypso (violet garters, babes lost in the wood, lovely seaside girls, the Track of the Sun, Boylan's letter, Milly's letter about a young student in Mullingar, Molly's father, Matcham's Masterstroke, the homerule sun, metempsychosis, the Conroys, the bee-sting, scapulars, the mezuzah on the doorpost, Agendath Netaim), Lotus Eaters (alcoholic men, M'Coy, the Belfast concert tour, Leah, Martha's letter, Molly's perfume, Mary and Martha, Prescott's, the bath, weight, the Cinghalese, high school science, the Gold Cup), Hades (houses of mourning, women washing corpses, Dan Dawson's speech, the man in the macintosh, snuff at a wake), Aeolus (the seder ritual), Lestrygonians (Burns on being seen, U.P.: Up, Guinness barges, the aria from The Huguenots), Scylla and Charybdis (the goddesses in the museum), Wandering Rocks (Boylan's spiffy clothes, AE and Lizzie Twigg, the Glencree dinner), Sirens (Richie Goulding, the gassy cider), and Cyclops (Pill Lane, Barney Kiernan's, the City Arms hotel, furze, Nannetti's trip to London).

Never before in Ulysses has there been such a dense cluster of echoes of earlier textual events. The narrative innovation that Joyce makes here advances an important structural principle In the novel: "retrospective arrangement." In Wandering Rocks Tom Kernan uses this phrase to refer to the 1798 Rebellion, and Joyce has characters repeat the locution six more times in later chapters, suggesting that it is a key principle for reading his book. Starting with Nausicaa, the book itself starts to put the principle into action. Bloom's sleepy reflections on his day are followed two chapters later by the gigantic phantasmagoric recycling apparatus of Circe. Two chapters after that, Ithaca scans the day's accumulated experiences with the dispassionate detachment of an MRI machine, and in Penelope Molly approaches them with a new kind of eye—skeptical, appreciative, dismissive, hopeful, feminine.

John Hunt 2026
